comment: The note line of a published build: shown in builds/index.json, builds/index.html and (when the page already has a note banner) at the top of builds/<tag>/. tools/linux/builds-index.py applies it on every index rewrite. Changing a note line is the only change allowed to a published builds/ page (SPEC 17.11).

tabby-v1.5-rc2.text: Not promoted: a short run; one check of its test run failed on the test's own counting. The firmware is the same build as tabby-v1.5.

tabby-v1.5-rc1.text: Not promoted: a short run; one check of its test run failed on the test's own counting. An earlier build than tabby-v1.5.

tabby-v1.4-rc4.text: Not promoted: it made the device's screen pictures for the manual. The firmware is the same build as tabby-v1.4.

tabby-v1.4-rc3.text: Not promoted: three checks of the test run did not yet know the grace after the bar line. An earlier build than tabby-v1.4.

tabby-v1.4-rc2.text: Not promoted: the test run stopped at a new step (the release tool's fault). An earlier build than tabby-v1.4.

tabby-v1.4-rc1.text: Not promoted: it carried the input log onto the device for a soak. An earlier build than tabby-v1.4.

tabby-v1.3-rc5.text: Not promoted: three checks of the test run failed on the test's own conditions (a changed test song, the unit's mod wheel, a limit). The firmware is the same as tabby-v1.3.

tabby-v1.3-rc4.text: Not promoted: with a save due at the stop, MIDI Stop left 17 ms after SEQ PLAY (the limit is 15). Fixed in the next candidate.

tabby-v1.3-rc3.text: Not promoted: its test run was stopped; a MIDI Stop could wait behind a save sent right after it. Fixed in the next candidate.

tabby-v1.3-rc2.text: Not promoted: on the ACTIONS page a soak segment's USB band was 3.54 ms (the page read the song storage while playing). Fixed in the next candidate.

tabby-v1.3-rc1.text: Not promoted: its waiting places for unsaved clips left the test tools' screen copy without memory. Fixed in the next candidate.

tabby-v1.2.1-rc2.text: Not promoted as it was: its manual still had simulator pictures. The firmware is the same build as tabby-v1.2.1.

tabby-v1.2.1-rc1.text: Not promoted: the comparison of the device's own screen pixels again found a row of the page before left on HOME after a page change while a song plays (the fix of tabby-v1.2 was not enough). tabby-v1.2.1 has it fixed.

tabby-v1.2-rc6.text: Not promoted: in one of 19 soak segments the song stayed in its second scene and played on the device's MIDI channels: a fault at SEQ PLAY that every earlier version has too (rare). tabby-v1.2 has it fixed.

tabby-v1.2-rc5.text: Not promoted: the comparison of the device's own screen pixels found pieces of the page before left on HOME after a page change while a song plays, and eight simultaneous lines measured 3.9 ms once on SCENES. Same firmware as tabby-v1.2-rc4. tabby-v1.2 has both fixed.

tabby-v1.2-rc4.text: Not promoted as it was: its manual still had simulator pictures, and three checks failed that were measured at the test computer while it was idle (docs/BUILD.md 65.4). The firmware is the same build as tabby-v1.2.

tabby-v1.2-rc3.text: Not promoted: one line of MIDI timing measured 2.3 to 2.5 ms on CLIPS and SCENES (the limit is under 2.0 ms): a change in this candidate moved the pages' repaints onto the eighth notes. It also shows the message CPU GUARD - VOICES ADAPTED over the page for as long as a song with many internal parts plays. tabby-v1.2 has both fixed.

tabby-v1.2-rc2.text: Not promoted: one line of MIDI timing measured 2.01 and 2.03 ms on two of eight pages (the limit is under 2.0 ms), and its screen copy showed that CLIPS and SCENES were being repainted on every 16th note while a song played. tabby-v1.2 has the fix.

tabby-v1.2-rc1.text: Not promoted: its screen copy (a test feature) asked the device for one block of 57600 bytes of memory and was refused, so the comparison of the device's pixels could not run; and one timing check of the CLIP SETTING test failed once (2.0 ms against 1.5 ms; 40 of 40 in three repeats on this build). Everything else passed. tabby-v1.2 itself has a smaller copy.

tabby-v04.3.text: Never released; superseded by tabby-v04.4. (An earlier note called it faulty; that was a measuring error.)

tabby-v04.5.text: Use tabby-v04.5.1 or later; this page cannot write v3 clips.

tabby-v04.10.text: Use tabby-v04.11.2 or later; on this page Full backup stops on a song that has a scene stored on the panel.

tabby-v04.11.text: Use tabby-v04.11.2 or later; on this page Full backup stops on a song that has a scene stored on the panel.

tabby-v04.11.1.text: Use tabby-v04.11.2 or later; on this page Full backup stops on a song that has a scene stored on the panel.

tabby-v04.15-rc1.text: Not promoted: device tests failed through errors in the test tools, not in the firmware (docs/BUILD.md 51.1, 51.2). The same firmware passed as tabby-v04.15-rc3.

tabby-v04.15-rc2.text: Not promoted: device tests failed through errors in the test tools, not in the firmware (docs/BUILD.md 51.2). The same firmware passed as tabby-v04.15-rc3.

tabby-v1.0.2-rc1.text: Not promoted: one check of one device test failed once and passed in two repeats; the likely cause is the test tool's clock. The firmware is the same build as tabby-v1.0.2-rc2.

tabby-v1.0.text: Use tabby-v1.0.1: in a song of two scenes that loops, this build (like tabby-v04.23, and probably every build before it) skips most of the scenes' program changes after the first pass.

tabby-v04.23-rc1.text: Not promoted: four device tests failed in the measuring (the test computer's clock was being corrected during the run, and one new check could not be aimed by remote). The firmware is the same build as tabby-v04.23-rc2.

tabby-v04.21-rc1.text: Not promoted: one device test failed through an error in the test tool (it pressed the wrong key). The firmware is the same build as tabby-v04.21-rc2.

tabby-v04.18-rc1.text: Not promoted: one timing check of the device tests read 4.21 ms against a limit of 4.0 ms that the test tool had set too tight (docs/BUILD.md 54.3). The same firmware passed as tabby-v04.18-rc2.
